newsitem.title: JORDAN: Arab Bank reports higher 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Arab Bank reports higher 1996 profit.

text.p: Arab Bank Group said on Friday its 1996 net profits rose 17.7 percent to $197.8 million, bolstered by a record performance from core business of Arab Bank Plc.

Arab Bank chairman Abdulmajeed Shoman said in an annual report distributed to shareholders the "outstanding financial results" were based largely on increased income from interest and commission on loans, and recovered bad debts.
Those increases more than offset a fall in foreign exchange trading revenue, he said.
Shareholders approved distribution of a four dinar dividend.

The Arab Bank Group includes Arab Bank Plc, its sister company Arab Bank (Switzerland) Ltd, the 100 percent owned banks Arab Bank Australia Ltd, Arab Bank (Austria) AG and Arab Bank AG in Frankfurt, and the 64.24 percent owned Arab Tunisian Bank.
Arab Bank Plc, one of the Middle East's major financial institutions, reported in January a record $135.2 million profit for 1996.
Shoman said total Arab Bank Group revenue before tax rose to $541.4 million in 1996 from $473.9 million the year before.
Pre-tax interest and commission revenue rose $43.7 million to $526.0 million last year, compensating for a $6.4 million fall in foreign exchange trading revenue.
Other revenues "improved significantly" to $41.5 million from $16.5 million, based on income from the group's trading portfolio, recovered bad debts and leasing of property.
Shoman said Arab Bank was still considering issuing a bonus share to shareholders but would wait for ratification of a law cancelling a 15 percent tax on capital increases.
